It is known that when a great beam rained down onto the land from on high, from the hidden citadel on the Moon, that a magic spread throughout the land. But such a raw magic, such unrefined power, was of no use to anyone. It was no more coherent than the chaos at the beginning of the universe, no better defined.

Fortunately, there is a force in nature that lends definition to chaos, that defies entropy and ushers creation. The Gods. And so it fell to Umbralocht to lend a little definition to this outburst.

The power of the beam permeates the air. It is an energy of high potential, a near-divine energy, ready to be transferred down to lesser forms. It is finite, though large: The beam fired once, and deposited its radiations into the air. They do not replenish naturally. This power would not dissipate naturally, either, and would take ages of regular down-conversion to sap. This energy, this mana of the world, flows in the air like currents. Sometimes more, sometimes less, and it changes with the winds. Those that seek to harness large quantities must chase the wind, or wait for favorable winds to come to them. Large use would sap the very air, and leave an area temporarily barren of mana, though this takes fair significant use.

What use? Well. the energies, they have a certain tendency to channel down along certain configurations of wire-like paths. Through chance, or through more specific intervention, there are such paths in most sentient beings. Some exceptions exist - for example, golems, which are too uniform and clay. (Unless they were to take to forging wires into themselves... Who can say.) These paths, these nerves, when stretched and lengthened and twisted into the correct shapes by use of sinew, muscle, proper movement, can resonate with mana, and grow heated. Hot, hotter, hotter! A typical resonance would make the nerves grow warm, and as they channel energy, grow warmer, soon cooking the sentient from inside.

This can be controlled. Through shaping and flensing one's nerves - something achievable through channeling small amounts of energy, until the excess burns away, via advanced meditation and flexing techniques yet undiscovered, or surgery, or through some twist of fortune happening to have one's nerves be just the right length and shape - one can make the resonance efficient, not converting into direct heat, but instead, into something else.

A given configuration of nerves, a shape, causes the higher-value energy of mana to flow through the shape and appear as another energy form, and, through delaying the conversion and creating a path to a target (the nerves make a beginning, where they point and converge marks an end) to appear in places other than the nerves. For example, it may be propelled then converted to heat, causing flame a distance from the nerves. It may be kinetic energy, causing distant motion. It may be local kinetic energy, causing a body to be shielded from impact, or flung in a direction. Local creation of energies can be useful.

An unskilled practitioner, a novice that has not much flensed their nerves, or bends them sub optimally and creates an unclean resonance, will get warm on the inside quickly. The better the mage, the cooler they run. Complex effects of energy manipulation require 'circuitry' in the flesh, that would have to be burned in, and then flexed with great precision to achieve specific manifestations. An illusion of a man is much harder than a point of fire, and requires complex circuitry indeed. For the illusion-man to move, requires great skill at moving the circuitry. Rawer, more directed manifestations - fire, lightning, kinetic movements - require less complicated circuitry, but directing them require precise movement, and high skill, all the same.

Further, the circuitry inside of people means that one cannot simply spawn fire inside of another, as the fire would be re-directed by their personal circuitry. however, by *touching* someone, one may link their nerves into a closed circuit that the one with the better know-how can manipulate. Achieving illusions through manifesting light-shows is hard, bordering on impractical: Achieving illusions by linking circuits with someone, and confusing their mind, is much easier. One can train one's circuitry to overcome others and project emotions, or cause damage, or to heal, if one's circuitry is correctly tuned to the species one is healing and one's skills and understandings let one compensate for the differences between individuals. No such advanced magics yet exist, as they would require much time and experimenting to discover - but they could.

Such configurations could theoretically be forged into objects, it a people were to develop such an art. Specific metals, specific configurations of metals would be required. How well they work would depend on the wind. With use, these, too, would become hot - perhaps melt, if made cheaply. Single-use, mass-produced stones that, when folded, project great heat until they slag themselves? Possible. More delicate, complex stones that, when twisted, project light and heat with no degradation, only needing to be turned off after a day of continuous use, and even then only for an hour? Harder.

Throughout the world, gradually, people would, knowingly or not, learn to take some advantage of this magic. Swords, for example, are a logical, if crude, extension of one's circuitry, and some swordsmen develop strange shapes of blocks and strange shapes of lunges that are more powerful than they physically should be, by adding kinetic effect. Thieves learn tricks with lock-picks to manipulate the insides of complex locks, through proper positioning. Chains are positioned to trap implausibly well, or to torture with heat, by the skilled. Etiquette is developed among nobility that lets one cut one's food with a fork, forks being a specially shaped piece of metal that converges cutting energies at the tip, cutting food yet harmless in a living mouth. Much of the internal heat generated by these more subtle activities are dismissed as 'sweating from exertion.'

Since the God of Ores and Metals is not around to protest: Some places of the world, ores naturally form into conductive circuitry, and as a result the areas near them are strange with strange energies.

#####[m] Here's a magic system! I can summarize and/or explain bits. I've been asked for a magic that allows for 'fire, telekenesis, and calming people.' Technically 'calming words' but I don't think that would make much sense given any of the current magics. Like, they could do that sort of thing with moon-god's magic, but that's 'divine,' not a 'mortal' magic. This form of magic does not rely on the gods, and ought to be able to do this.

#####I use a lot of words in this post, but the core tenants are reasonably simple: Wires are important, configurations of wires are important. Energy manifestation is easy, complex stuff like illusion or 'summons' is hard to impossible without way more infrastructure. 'Nerves' inside people count as wires. A bad configuration gets hot and melts, even a good configuration gets hot slowly, but the better you are the cooler you run. Mana is blown about in the winds, is finite, and can be used up in an area until more wind rolls it in. (Also it ebbs and flows with the weather.) So, no internal mana bar. Influencing a person with magic directly generally requires touching them. Getting 'good' at magic requires good muscle control, a flexible body, and a bunch of circuits carved into one's insides (probably by 'cooking them in' with magic, but you can start on this with just naturally occurring configurations of nerves). 'Wands' and other tools are helpful because they extend one's circuitry. Basic stuff like keys, lockpicks, swords, have some circuit-extending properties, as well, and with a lot of skill also let one do some neat stuff, so this magic's not just for wizards. Throwing piles of twisty wires everywhere makes magic really hard to do.
